page: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and includes 24 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 21.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.62 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most standard compute and memory operations. The instance achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core, Passmark CPU, and static web serving throughput tests. However, multi-core execution shows limitations, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the weak category. Similarly, LLM inference tasks represent a performance bottleneck, with prompt processing on a 7B model rated as poor and text generation on the same model rated as weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.2xlarge offers a dedicated CPU allocation and DDR4 memory profile tailored for network-heavy compute tasks without the overhead of bundled local storage. Given its average database operation and Redis SET performance, alongside its 10 Gbps baseline network speed, this server is suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and network-bound utility tasks, whereas it is less suited for intensive multi-threaded processing or large-scale machine learning inference.
